about: respd's application mutants; each is judged by the example's laws, tests, explore leg and cases (scripts/examples), not by a compiler test.

mutants.name: resp-parse-accepts-short-bulk
mutants.to: let stop = try lineEnd(buf, start, MaxBulk)
mutants.rule: A bulk string is the count of bytes its header says, then CRLF: a parser that ends it at the next CRLF reads data shorter than its length as a value. BulkTakesItsLength and SplitAnywhereParsesTheSame refute it.

mutants.name: resp2-writes-resp3-null
mutants.rule: RESP2 has no null type; it writes null as the null bulk string. The reader reads both as Null, so only Resp2WritesOnlyItsOwnTypes (resp/tests.ergo) sees it.

mutants.name: memory-incr-reads-then-writes
mutants.from:
let r = sync.Modify(shard(e, key)) func(m Map[string, Entry]) (Counted, Map[string, Entry]) {
		let old = find(m, key, now)
mutants.rule: Incr reads and writes its key in one Modify; a read before it lets two tasks write the same sum. The laws run one task and pass it; the explore leg of IncrIsAtomic finds the schedule.

mutants.name: lease-release-ignores-token
mutants.origin: wf10 plan §8 (verifier must see it killed by a law)
mutants.rule: A release frees a name only with the grant's token: an owner whose lease expired and who acquired the name again must not free the new grant with the old lease. ReleaseNeedsTheToken refutes it.

mutants.name: lease-token-reset-on-expiry
mutants.origin: wf10 plan §8 (verifier must see it killed by a law)
mutants.rule: An expired grant keeps its token as the name's last, so the next grant's token is greater. TokensRise refutes a counter that starts again.

mutants.name: memory-expiry-holds-at-its-time
mutants.rule: A key is Missing from its expiry on, the expiry's own instant included. ExpiredIsMissing refutes an engine that holds the value at that instant.

mutants.name: decimal-accepts-leading-zero
mutants.rule: Incr reads a value as Redis does: no leading zero and no -0. DecimalReadsItsText refutes a reader that takes 07.
